newsitem.title: FRANCE: Framatome denies preparing Westinghouse unit bid.
newsitem.headline: Framatome denies preparing Westinghouse unit bid.

text.p: French nuclear engineering group Framatome on Tuesday denied formally a newspaper report saying it was preparing a bid for Westinghouse Electric Corp energy division.
"Framatome denies formally a newspaper article saying it is preparing a bid for a Westinghouse unit," Philippe Raulin, the company's secretary-general, told Reuters.
Daily newspaper Liberation said on Tuesday that GEC Alsthom was preparing a joint bid with Framatome for the Westinghouse unit.
GEC Alsthom had no immediate comment. GEC Alsthom is a joint-venture of Alcatel Alsthom and GEC Plc.
Alcatel also has a 44 percent stake in Framatome, the rest being controlled by French state entities.

Merger talks between GEC Alsthom and Framatome were ended in April "After the British shareholder of GEC Alsthom and the public shareholder of Framatome decided a merger was not possible under the present conditions," Raulin said.

Liberation said that GEC Alsthom had lodged a joint bid with Framatome on July 25. The newspaper carried photocopies of what it said were working documents for a bid by GEC Alsthom and Framatome for the Westinghouse division, which it said comprises 80 nuclear centres.
Liberation said the division was worth between $1.47 and $1.55 billion.
The paper said that on July 7, a French delegation led by Pierre Bilger, head of GEC Alsthom, had met Westinghouse executives in the United States.
The US group plans to split its media and industrial operations into separate companies in September this year.
Liberation quoted a source close to the talks as saying that Framatome, which has funds of 10 billion francs, would take on the nuclear risk, estimated at between 750 and 900 million dollars.
It said the cost of the deal would be between zero and $300 million after the risk and debts had been taken into account.
